title: Fair Measure

serves.summary: The learner fixes a row of units under a ribbon so they are the same size, end to end, with no gaps or overlaps, then types the length, which shows they can measure length fairly with same-sized units.

request.topic: Measuring length fairly with same-sized units
request.objective: Measure a length with same-sized units laid end to end, with no gaps or overlaps, and say why mixed units give a wrong count.

problems.ask: Someone tried to measure this ribbon with blocks, but it is not a fair measure yet. Fix it, then type how many blocks long the ribbon is.
problems.goal: Four blocks end to end from the start line to the end line, and 4 typed. The laid blocks have a gap.

problems.ask: These clips do not make a fair measure yet. Fix them, then type how many clips long the ribbon is.
problems.goal: Six clips end to end across the ribbon, and 6 typed. The first two clips overlap, so the row stops short.

problems.ask: This row reaches the end of the ribbon, but it is not a fair measure. Fix it, then type how long the ribbon is.
problems.goal: One kind of unit end to end across the ribbon, and that number typed. The laid row mixes blocks and clips and has no gaps.

problems.ask: Measure this ribbon fairly with the units in the tray, then type how long it is.
problems.goal: Four blocks or eight clips end to end, and that number typed. Mixed units do not count.
